Seminar Title:

Design and Development of an Intelligent Auto-Alignment Free Space Optical Communication System Using Adaptive Channel Estimation Techniques

Seminar Type:

Registration Seminar

Department:

Electronics and Communication Engineering

Speaker Name:

Suchitra Rana ( Rollno : 523ec6013)

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

EC Seminar Hall, EC303

Date and Time:

18 Nov 2026 10.30

Contact:

Santos Kumar Das

Abstract:

Free-space optical (FSO) communication is a promising complement to radio-frequency backhaul in fifth- and sixth-generation (5G and 6G) networks, offering unlicensed spectrum and multi-gigabit data rates. Intensity modulation and direct detection (IM/DD)-based optical orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM), particularly DC-biased optical OFDM (DCO-OFDM) and asymmetrically clipped optical OFDM (ACO-OFDM), enables the generation of real-valued, non-negative optical signals. However, outdoor FSO links are severely affected by path loss, atmospheric attenuation, Gamma-Gamma turbulence, pointing errors, partial blockage, and physical obstructions, resulting in highly dynamic channel conditions and challenging channel state information (CSI) acquisition. Conventional least-squares (LS) and statistical estimation techniques have limitations under such conditions, while sparse recovery methods remain insufficiently explored for both DCO-OFDM and ACO-OFDM under a unified composite channel model.

This research aims to develop an intelligent auto-alignment FSO communication system using adaptive channel estimation to maintain reliable connectivity under dynamic atmospheric and pointing conditions. As the first phase, a unified channel estimation framework is developed to incorporate multiple physical deployment scenarios into a common observation model. Six estimation techniques, namely LS, interpolated LS, discrete Fourier transform (DFT)-based, linear minimum mean-square error (LMMSE), practical minimum mean-square error (MMSE), and orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP), are formulated and evaluated against perfect CSI. Their performance is analyzed in terms of mean-square error (MSE), normalized MSE (NMSE), bit error rate (BER), average data rate, and outage probability. Analytical results are validated through extensive Monte Carlo simulations. The results demonstrate that OMP achieves estimation accuracy close to the perfect CSI benchmark and outperforms conventional estimators under both nominal and severe atmospheric conditions. Future work will integrate adaptive channel estimates into an intelligent auto-alignment mechanism for real-time pointing-error detection and correction, followed by system prototyping and experimental validation.
